title: Short Form Video for Real Estate Agents: What to Film Each Week and How to Tell It Is Working
seoTitle: Short Form Video for Real Estate Agents
seoDescription: A simple weekly short form video system for real estate agents: five video types to rotate, how to batch film, Fair Housing pitfalls to avoid and the numbers that show it is working.
excerpt: Clients want a feel for you before they call. A simple weekly video routine, five formats to rotate, and the signals that matter more than views.
imageAlt: Man kneeling on a living room floor filming himself with a smartphone mounted on a gimbal
imageIdea: Real photo of a person recording vertical video with a phone on a stand or gimbal indoors, no readable screen or logos.
author: Michael Shad, Founder of The SocialDM
bodyHtml:
Short form video is the fastest way for someone to get a feel for you before they ever call. A buyer who has watched you walk through three neighborhoods, or a seller who has seen how you show a home, already has a sense of whether they like you. That matters because most clients still come through people who know you, and a referred client almost always looks you up first.

The problem is that most agent video is either too polished to keep up or too random to build anything. Here is a simple weekly system.

What should you film?

Rotate through five types. Each one answers a question a buyer or seller already has.

VideoWhat it showsWho it is for
Neighborhood minuteOne street, park, coffee shop or school route, and who it suitsBuyers comparing areas, people relocating
Listing walk throughThe home in the order a buyer would see it, with one honest detail per roomBuyers, and sellers judging how you market
Market readOne local number this month, such as days on market, and what it meansSellers deciding when to list, past clients
Process explainerOne step, such as inspections or appraisal gaps, in under a minuteFirst time buyers and nervous sellers
Client storyWhat the client needed and how it worked out, with their permissionAnyone deciding whether to trust you

Use local numbers from your MLS and say where they came from. A clear number from your market is more useful than a national headline.

How do you keep it up every week?

  • Batch film. Pick one morning every two weeks. Film four to six videos in one area or one listing. Edit in one sitting.
  • Use the same structure. Open with the question or the place in the first second, give the answer, end with one simple next step: "message me for the full list."
  • Talk to one person. Picture a specific past client and talk to them. It sounds more natural and keeps you from rambling.
  • Add captions. Many people watch with the sound off.
  • Post the same video in more than one place. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Facebook, plus your Google Business Profile when it fits. A good neighborhood video can also live on that area's page on your website.

What should you avoid?

  • Describing who a home or area is "perfect for" in terms of people. The Fair Housing Act's ban on discriminatory statements applies to all advertising, and social video counts. Describe the property and the place, not the kind of people who should live there (HUD advertising guidance).
  • Filming a listing without written permission. Get the seller's sign off, follow your brokerage and MLS rules, and keep personal items, security systems and family photos out of frame.
  • Trending audio that hides your voice. For agents, you are the reason to watch.
  • Chasing views. A video with a few hundred views from people in your town is worth more than a viral one from people who will never move there.

How do you tell if it is working?

Views tell you if people saw it. These tell you if it is building business:

  1. Saves and shares. People keep or pass along what is useful.
  2. Profile visits and follows from your area. Check your audience location in each app's insights.
  3. Messages and website clicks. The step right before a conversation.
  4. What new clients tell you. Ask every new client, "Did you watch any of my videos before you called?" and log it in your CRM. After six months that answer tells you more than any dashboard.

Give a format at least eight weeks before you judge it. Then do more of what gets saved, shared and mentioned by clients, and drop the rest.

Video is one part of the plan. I covered the rest in Real Estate Agent Marketing Plan for 2027. At The SocialDM, short form video is the core of our work for agents, and you can see how it fits with LocalLift Signature.

Questions we hear

How often should a real estate agent post short form video?

Two or three times a week is enough for most agents if you keep it up all year. Film several in one session so it does not take over your week.

Do I need professional video equipment?

No. A recent phone, a small stand or gimbal, a clip on microphone and daylight cover most of it. Clear sound matters more than a perfect picture.

Can I post videos of my listings?

Get the seller's written permission, check your brokerage and MLS rules, and confirm your photographer's license covers social use if you use their footage. Keep personal items and anything that identifies the owners out of frame.

How do I know if video is bringing business?

Watch saves, shares, profile visits, messages and website clicks, then ask every new client what they watched before calling. Views alone do not tell you much.

takeaways: Rotate five video types: neighborhood minute, listing walk through, market read, process explainer and client story.
Batch film four to six videos every two weeks so the routine survives a busy month.
Describe the property and the place, not the people who should live there, to stay within Fair Housing rules.
Judge video by saves, shares, local profile visits, messages and what new clients tell you, not by views.
